evals.name: greenfield-full-brief
evals.prompt: I'm starting a new app called Pulse — it's an analytics dashboard for indie SaaS founders to track MRR, churn and trials. Vite + React 19 + Tailwind 4, no component library yet. Our brand colour is #4F46E5. I really like how Linear looks — the density and the calm. Yes I want it to feel animated. Set up the design.
evals.expected_output: A greenfield planning phase that ends at Gate 1: docs/design/ui-options.html plus 3-5 option-tokens/*.css, every option contrast-clean, options genuinely distinct on surface kit and font pairing, names rewritten from the generated style-row names into editorial ones, brand hex pinned as --primary in every option, and a closing message asking the user to name a letter. No UI-PLAN.md, no scaffold, no app code.
assertions: Produced a tabbed option preview HTML under docs/design/
Seeded 3-5 named directions rather than proposing a single theme
Used the skill's seed-options.py generator instead of hand-authoring palettes
Every option token file clears contrast-check.mjs with zero FAILs
No option carries a WARN on --ring (an invisible focus indicator ships as an accessibility bug)
Every option pins the user's brand colour #4F46E5 as --primary
No two options share the same --surface-* kit, so the set is not hue variants
No two options share the same font pairing
Motion personalities are spread across the set rather than repeating one or two
No option previews as 'still' when the user asked for animation
Every option ships a derived dark theme alongside light
Option names read as directions, not as raw style-row technique names like 'Neumorphism'
The preview renders the dashboard archetype, matching the analytics-console brief
The Linear reference the user pasted is carried into the preview brief
Gate 2 held: no app scaffold, no src/ tree, no index.css written before plan approval
Gate 1 held: no UI-PLAN.md written before the user named an option
The closing message asks the user to pick a direction by letter

evals.name: themed-app-refresh-gate
evals.prompt: our dashboard theme feels dated, can you make it look better? we're staying on react and tailwind.
evals.expected_output: Probe run against the existing React 19 / Tailwind 4 app, THEMED verdict reported naming src/index.css and the 5 components in src/components/ui, detected versions stated back for confirmation, and the refresh-vs-replacement question asked. src/index.css byte-identical, no options seeded before the answer exists.
files: project/ (React 19.2.8 + Tailwind 4.3.3 app with a themed src/index.css, 5 ui components, and prior docs/design/ work)
assertions: Ran the context probe before asking the user anything
Reported the THEMED verdict rather than treating the app as unthemed
Named the existing token file src/index.css in the report
Named the component directory src/components/ui and its file count
Stated the detected React and Tailwind versions back for confirmation
Asked refresh vs replacement, spelling out what each one means
Left src/index.css byte-identical
Left the entire project untouched — no file added, modified, or removed
Read the existing screen files for layout conventions worth preserving
Seeded no options and wrote no plan before the refresh/replacement answer exists

evals.name: underspecified-no-inference
evals.prompt: make my landing page look good, im using react
evals.expected_output: An interview turn only. Runs the probe, then asks the three stack questions (FE framework, UI framework offered from the React-valid row of the matrix, styling engine + major) and either asks or explicitly defers the four concept questions — the skill sends the stack group together and the concept questions one at a time after it. Asks nothing about fonts, radius, density, mood or light-vs-dark. No shadcn install, no colours chosen, no token or component file written.
assertions: Ran the context probe before asking the user anything
Asked which UI/component framework rather than inferring one from 'react'
Offered only React-compatible UI frameworks from the compatibility matrix
Asked the styling engine and its major version
Did not treat shadcn/ui as settled just because the stack is React
Asked nothing about fonts, corner radius, density, spacing, mood, or light-vs-dark
Either asked the four concept questions or explicitly deferred them — not skipped
Chose no colours and wrote no token file, component, or CSS
Seeded no options before the concept answers exist
Did not silently default the stack or proceed on an assumed answer
